wire.title: Kessel Valley line to close for six weeks of bridge repairs
paragraphs: The Kessel Valley railway line will close for six weeks from 3 November while engineers repair a damaged bridge near Harrow Bridge station, the operator said on Monday.
The line carries about 1,200 commuters a day between Harrow Bridge and the coast, and replacement buses will run every 20 minutes during the closure.
Kessel Rail said the bridge had been damaged by flooding in September and that inspections had found erosion around two of its supports.
The operator apologised for the disruption and said the work could not be put off without risking a longer closure in the depths of winter.
Season ticket holders will be offered a refund for the weeks the line is shut, the company said, with details to be published on its website.
Local MP Dana Whitlow said she had asked the transport department to make sure replacement services were accessible for disabled passengers.

gazette.title: Six-week rail shutdown: what Kessel Valley commuters need to know
paragraphs: Commuters in the lower valley face a difficult autumn, and the Gazette has gathered what we know about how the closure will affect journeys into the city.
The Kessel Valley railway line will close for six weeks from 3 November while engineers repair a damaged bridge near Harrow Bridge station, the operator said on Monday.

day2.title: Kessel Valley closure pushed back a week
paragraphs: The Kessel Valley railway line will close for six weeks from 10 November while engineers repair a damaged bridge near Harrow Bridge station, the operator said on Monday.
The line carries about 1,200 commuters a day between Harrow Bridge and the coast, and replacement buses will run every 30 minutes during the closure.
Kessel Rail said the bridge had been damaged by flooding in September and that inspections had found erosion around two of its supports.
Kessel Rail said the one-week delay would give bus companies more time to recruit drivers for the replacement service.
Local MP Dana Whitlow said she had asked the transport department to make sure replacement services were accessible for disabled passengers.
